questions.prompt: A Claude subagent reads 30 files. What returns to the parent agent?

options.text: All 30 files, so the parent can check the work
options.explanation: Intermediate tool calls and results stay inside the subagent.
Right. That is the context isolation benefit: the parent gets a summary, not every file.

options.text: Nothing: the parent must read the subagent's transcript
options.explanation: The final message is returned to the parent as the Agent tool's result.

questions.prompt: In the OpenAI Agents SDK, how does the model see a handoff to an agent named `Refund Agent`?

options.explanation: Right. Handoffs are represented as tools to the model.

options.text: As a new system prompt that replaces the current one
options.explanation: The model calls a tool to hand off. The runner then switches agents.

options.text: It does not see it; your code routes by keyword
options.explanation: That would be orchestration in code. A handoff is a choice the model makes through a tool.

questions.prompt: Per Anthropic's research system post, which task suits a multi-agent design best?

options.text: A short bug fix in one function
options.explanation: The post says most coding tasks have fewer truly parallel parts than research.

options.text: A breadth-first research question with many independent directions
options.explanation: Right. The post says multi-agent systems excel at heavy parallelization and information that exceeds one context window.

options.text: A task where every step depends on the step before
options.explanation: The post says domains with many dependencies between agents are not a good fit today.
